author: Codex assessment agent /root/liberal_conservative (AI-assisted doctrinal interpretation)
changeNote: Completed 240 independently considered answers to the current bank from the scoped doctrine. No imported 12Axes vectors or score targets. User authorised neutral answers and completion on 2026-10-04. Conditional modern applications and mixed-causation modelling are explicitly inferred, not claims of direct statements or scientific findings. Independent review completed on 2026-10-04; question-meaning and evidence corrections are recorded in review notes.

metadata.name: Thatcherism
metadata.description: The political-economic doctrine developed by the Thatcher/Joseph movement, with privatisation, market competition, legal order and national sovereignty. Historical government conduct is contextual evidence rather than an automatic doctrinal position.
metadata.scope: The political-economic doctrine developed by the Thatcher/Joseph movement, with privatisation, market competition, legal order and national sovereignty. Historical government conduct is contextual evidence rather than an automatic doctrinal position. This is a representative interpretation of the specified doctrine, not answers personally submitted by every adherent. Modern technological questions apply the doctrine conditionally. Trait-specific neutral responses express a stated mixed-causation model where the doctrine rejects a single fixed causal priority; they are not empirical scientific estimates.
metadata.phrase: A society based on private ownership, competitive enterprise, personal responsibility and a state maintaining law and national defence.

sources.title: Speech in Korea: The Principles of Thatcherism
Speech concluding Saving the Ozone Layer Conference
Right to buy: Past, present and future

axes.brief: Thatcher's stated principles combine parliamentary sovereignty, elections and independent courts.
axes.counterEvidence: Her assertive governing style is not an expressed power to abolish parliament or electoral accountability.

answers.rationale: Free elections are among the stated constitutional title deeds.
Technocratic appointment cannot replace electoral authority.
Modern parliamentary citizenship includes universal adult voting.
Parliamentary supremacy excludes executive lawmaking against parliament.
Political freedom requires an opposition able to compete.
Parliamentary financial accountability limits executive spending power.
Independent courts are explicitly defended against executive control.
Union leadership cannot replace the electorate's political authority.
Political opposition cannot be excluded merely for disagreement.
Parliamentary deliberation is preferred to routine plebiscitary repeal.
Strong prime-ministerial leadership remains constitutionally accountable.
Defined parliamentary removal protects the constitutional order.
Continuity is not a licence to suspend electoral choice.
Accountability and representative independence require institutional balance.
Unaccountable leadership contradicts the stated constitutional principles.
Military intervention would displace the constitutional civilian order.

axes.brief: Liberty is sustained by law, strong policing and individual responsibility.
axes.counterEvidence: Economic freedom is not equivalent to unrestricted conduct; due process remains a stated constitutional value.

answers.rationale: Responsibility and social order qualify unrestricted harmful personal choices.
Judicial surveillance authority supports effective lawful policing.
Obstruction conflicts with protecting others' lawful access and work.
Free political criticism remains part of constitutional liberty.
Individual responsibility generally outweighs compulsory self-protection.
Security utility competes with legal protection against intrusive government.
Preventing harm on public roads fits lawful order.
A judicially established threat warrants proportionate restriction.
Freedom of expression and traditional public morality compete.
Private communication should normally remain outside routine state registration.
Credible violence can justify exceptional preventive policing.
Preventing serious public disorder is a core state function.
Independent courts should protect homes from arbitrary search.
Official accountability competes with confidentiality and national security.
Self-defence and public safety require regulated rather than categorical treatment.
Unreviewable indefinite detention exceeds rule-of-law restraint.

axes.brief: Shared British institutions, national loyalty and traditional civic culture receive priority.
axes.counterEvidence: Individual liberty permits private diversity; historical national rhetoric does not establish a uniform coercive cultural policy.

answers.rationale: Shared national institutions take priority in public conflicts.
Access accommodation is legitimate where cost and cohesion remain proportionate.
Settlement entails meaningful participation in common national customs.
Private heritage is tolerated within strong national identification.
A common public language supports civic participation.
Historical recognition is acceptable without elevating group identity over citizenship.
Public support should sustain established national traditions.
Common national membership should not yield automatically to sectional identity.
Shared public routines help preserve national cohesion.
Plural traditions can coexist within a predominantly common civic identity.
Integration should enable active participation in the wider nation.
Language assistance is practical where it promotes participation.
Family socialisation should sustain national belonging.
Religious freedom and generally necessary public rules require balancing.
Private plurality is accepted without replacing common national culture.
Integration should emphasise shared institutions and civic customs.

axes.brief: National sovereignty and social cohesion support controlled immigration with lawful exceptions.
axes.counterEvidence: Market openness and individual opportunity do not imply unrestricted settlement.

answers.rationale: Intake planning should reflect national capacity and needs.
A wish to improve living standards does not itself confer entry rights.
Economic usefulness matters alongside family and humanitarian claims.
Immediate family unity supports responsible settled households.
Humanitarian duties require consideration with security and settlement capacity.
Unlawful entry does not create a general right to remain.
National policy may limit immigration despite employer demand.
Housing and service capacity can justify restraint.
Family admissions should be considered within national intake planning.
Employment supports admission but is not sufficient by itself.
Established sponsors help demonstrate responsibility and viable settlement.

Controlled admission based on economic need and established ties favours a work or family route rather than graduation alone as the qualifying basis. This is an inferred selection rule, not a claim that a pathway guarantees residence.
Protection against persecution can justify exceptional admission.
Practical integration may matter without automatic preference by cultural origin.
Established lawful residents can qualify while new arrivals face conditions.
Increasing cultural difference is not an independent migration objective.

axes.brief: Deterrence, NATO and opposition to appeasement require strong conventional and nuclear defence.
axes.counterEvidence: Negotiation and verified arms reductions remain possible from strength; this is not war for its own sake.

answers.rationale: Force may be necessary to protect interests and defeat aggression.
Diplomacy is useful but cannot always precede timely defensive action.
Military strength is explicitly treated as the basis of secure peace.
Imminent attack can justify preventive defence.
Collective security may require more than narrow retaliation.
Professional capability is preferable without a demonstrated conscription emergency.
Major appeasement risks encouraging further aggression.
Advanced defence technology is supported, subject to effective control.
Homeland defence coexists with alliance and overseas responsibilities.
Abandoning an attacked ally contradicts staunch alliance support.
Credible alliances need sustained combat capability beyond home borders.

Unresolved territorial claims alone do not justify initiating war. Thatcher’s defence of the Falklands campaign concerns responding to an invasion; that counterexample does not establish approval of starting a war merely to settle a dispute.
Credible threats can deter coercion and protect national interests.
Firm resolve is viewed as preventing larger future wars.
Intelligence advantage strengthens deterrence despite diplomatic risks.
Negotiated reductions are acceptable when security remains credible.

axes.brief: National sovereignty coexists with NATO, trade cooperation and defence of the free world.
axes.counterEvidence: Thatcher's international engagement should not be confused with support for political federation or shared monetary control.

answers.rationale: National constitutional institutions retain final authority.
External bodies should not override fundamental national decisions.
Domestic constitutional authority must constrain external legal demands.
NATO commitments are explicitly and strongly defended.
Sovereignty includes the ability to withdraw from international arrangements.
External judicial power must not erode national constitutional responsibility.
National sovereignty receives priority against institutional encroachment.
Environmental cooperation is useful without unrestricted external authority.
A compulsory common foreign policy can constrain necessary national judgment.
Human rights matter while external lawmaking remains constitutionally constrained.
The critique of monetary shadowing supports retaining currency control.
Shared projects can serve national and allied interests.
National government should retain decisive border responsibility.
Common trade rules can strengthen free exchange.
Political federation conflicts with defended national sovereignty.
Allied defence of common rules can outweigh immediate material benefit.

axes.brief: Privatisation spreads property and subjects firms to commercial discipline.
axes.counterEvidence: Public schools, hospitals and roads remain legitimate spending priorities in the cited speech; this is not total privatisation.

answers.rationale: Private enterprise is the principal creator of wealth.
Water, gas and electricity privatisation are explicitly defended.
Equivalent outcomes favour private ownership and independence.
Routine state enterprise extends government beyond its proper framework role.
Public hospitals remain legitimate alongside private healthcare choice.
Historical rail arrangements and broader privatisation principles pull differently.
Competitive delivery should free taxpayers from inefficient administration.
Ordinary public banks lack the normal presumption for enterprise.
Selling commercial state assets is a defining commitment.
Wider private homeownership is preferred to extensive council ownership.
Effective security regulation permits private strategic enterprise.
Natural-resource businesses generally belong in private enterprise.
Privatised refuse collection is explicitly cited as desirable.
Security alone does not require ownership when other safeguards suffice.
Privatisation should end repeated taxpayer rescue of inefficient management.
Public-service broadcasting and market plurality can coexist pragmatically.

axes.brief: Competition and enterprise favour open trade and opposition to protected inefficiency.
axes.counterEvidence: Defence and fair-competition exceptions qualify pure unilateral free trade.

answers.rationale: Sheltering uncompetitive producers weakens enterprise discipline.
Lower barriers expose firms to productive competition.
Routine national preference can waste taxpayers' resources.
Enterprises should ordinarily obtain inputs on competitive terms.
Critical defence resilience may justify selected safeguards.
Domestic consumers can benefit from unilateral liberalisation.
Infant-industry protection risks preserving dependency on government.
Foreign investment generally expands competition and productive capacity.
Permanent agricultural shelter weakens market adjustment.
Uncompetitive firms should adapt rather than rely on protection.
Retaliation is a tactical option, not a general economic principle.
Origin-neutral taxes support competitive markets.
Distorting foreign subsidies can warrant proportionate countermeasures.
Open trade agreements generally outweigh self-sufficiency preferences.
Genuine security risks can justify strategic investment screening.
Digital services inherit the presumption of free exchange.

axes.brief: Competition, market prices and monetary discipline replace state economic direction.
axes.counterEvidence: Government still sets legal frameworks and provides public goods; sound money is a state responsibility in the primary speech.

answers.rationale: Private enterprise should determine ordinary output.
Mandatory production targets conflict with market coordination.
Supply and demand should generally determine prices.
National production plans displace decentralised enterprise judgment.
The speech explicitly rejects rescuing uncompetitive firms from closure.
Price controls frustrate market adjustment and supply incentives.
Reducing entry barriers encourages new enterprise.
Political credit direction conflicts with independent commercial allocation.
Capital freedom fits rejection of economic controls.
Selected subsidies usually entrench inefficient interests.
The speech assigns government responsibility for sound money rather than competing currencies.
Mandated wage floors risk excluding less productive workers in this model.
Labour bargaining should not become a state wage schedule.
Monetary policy should secure stability rather than finance an economic plan.
Market rents favour private supply and investment.
Comprehensive coordination reproduces the collectivism explicitly rejected.

axes.brief: Tax cuts, property and responsibility coexist with necessary public protection.
axes.counterEvidence: The primary speech endorses schools, roads and hospitals; this does not entail strong cash equalisation.

answers.rationale: Substantial income compression conflicts with reward for enterprise.
Unequal earnings alone do not justify taking additional income.
Higher-tax benefit expansion threatens incentives and fiscal discipline.
A basic safety net is preferable to broad levelling.
Steep progression conflicts with criticism of penal income-tax rates.
Retaining earnings encourages work, saving and investment.
Intergenerational property supports family responsibility and independence.
Work-oriented limits can reinforce personal responsibility.
Accumulated property should not generally fund extensive equalisation.
Taxpayer burdens legitimately constrain benefit generosity.
Dignity matters, but broader participation support must preserve incentives.
Cutting tax burdens is a central programme commitment.
Targeted work support may help, but subsidy dependency is a concern.
Lower marginal-rate differences support productive effort.
Land redistribution conflicts with security and spread of voluntary property ownership.
Cash assistance should principally address genuine need.

axes.brief: Moral responsibility and inherited Christian public culture coexist with civil parliamentary authority.
axes.counterEvidence: Personal faith does not establish support for a clerical veto or religious courts.

answers.rationale: Parliamentary law needs civic justification even when morally religiously informed.
Religious moral inheritance is valued without making scripture a binding code.
The elected government does not require religious leaders' permission.
Historic Christian constitutional recognition fits inherited British institutions.
Shared education and inherited Christian teaching require accommodation of conscience.
Traditional faith education is accepted with respect for family conscience.
Independent civil courts apply the law of the constitutional state.
Inherited advisory roles differ from a general clerical approval requirement.
Traditional worship can form part of state ceremony.
Heritage and voluntary religious service differ from state conversion policy.
Inherited religious symbols can express national continuity.
Christian festivals are part of established national institutions.
Historic clerical representation competes with reform and electoral accountability.
Voluntary religious institutions can merit special fiscal protection.
Civil marriage should remain possible without religious consent.
Binding parallel religious courts risk fragmenting common civil law.

axes.brief: Responsibility, family stability and inherited moral institutions temper economic radicalism.
axes.counterEvidence: Reforming markets does not imply social progressivism, while individual achievement qualifies rigid sex-role prescriptions.

answers.rationale: Useful adaptation is allowed without abandoning inherited moral frameworks.
Established moral traditions deserve priority over transient cultural fashion.
Family dignity extends broadly while the married model remains preferred.
Family tradition coexists with individual ability and achievement.
The historical doctrine largely retains the established heterosexual marriage model.
Stable married families are central to responsibility across generations.
Early abortion involves competing conscience, autonomy and moral concerns.
Parents retain major responsibility for moral and sexual upbringing.
Historical family complementarity weighs against equivalent adoption recognition.
Conventional public modesty fits inherited moral restraint.
Established usage is preferred over rapid identity-driven language revision.
Transmitting responsibility and established values is central to family life.
Individual achievement can legitimately cross conventional role expectations.
Social institutions require more gradual change than failing economic arrangements.
Parental moral expectations qualify compulsory teaching of new sexual norms.
Continuity across generations is a substantive value.

axes.brief: Enterprise and scientific advance support innovation; the 1989 ozone-conference speech supports environmental responsibility.
axes.counterEvidence: Environmental risks and human enhancement require distinct judgments rather than being inferred solely from economic deregulation.

answers.rationale: Beneficial technology should develop under proportionate legal safeguards.
Waiting for broad long-term certainty can obstruct useful enterprise.
Important infrastructure can justify limited managed habitat loss.
Medical exposure requires adequate safety evidence.
Innovation and competitive productivity favour AI adoption with retraining.
Preservation should not categorically veto important development.
New food production must be assessed for practical safety and benefit.
Permanent invasive enhancement warrants stronger evidence.
Scientific progress is a major means of addressing environmental problems.
Investigation is necessary, but delay must remain proportionate.
Adult responsibility and irreversible implant risks require balance.
Clinical reliability should be established before routine diagnosis.
Heritable enhancement raises distinct moral concerns beyond ordinary innovation.
Durable ecosystem exposure justifies careful testing.
Housing and infrastructure support opportunity with environmental safeguards.
Irreversible damage merits a higher evidential threshold.

axes.brief: Parliamentary sovereignty and national economic reform constrain local autonomy.
axes.counterEvidence: Market decentralisation is distinct from territorial decentralisation; actual local-government controls qualify localist rhetoric.

answers.rationale: Local initiative matters but lacks immunity from sovereign parliamentary reform.
Parliamentary national authority resolves competing territorial claims.
National continuity outweighs an automatic regional exit entitlement.
National reform may override obstructive local policy.
Regional institutions are permissible but not sovereign against parliament.
Local police accountability coexists with common national law and standards.
National fiscal discipline can constrain retention and local expenditure.
Common educational standards can justify national requirements.
Local taxation exists but remains subject to national constraints.
National employment law implements a common competitive framework.
Local boundaries and powers remain subject to national legislation.
National public healthcare requires common entitlement rules.
Local institutions are possible within common individual rights and national law.
National limits can protect taxpayers against local fiscal excess.
Purely local land effects favour local practical judgment.
Multi-region emergencies require decisive national coordination.

axes.brief: Innate talents coexist with enterprise, learned responsibility and institutional incentives.
axes.counterEvidence: The speech's reference to innate ability does not rank races or establish biological causation for every trait.

answers.rationale: Innate dispositions and learned responsibility both contribute to conduct.

International IQ comparisons involve education, health, measurement and inheritance; the scoped doctrine does not assign a stable causal priority. This representative response adopts a mixed model rather than inferring biology from citizenship or tradition.
Sex differences may involve biology and socially learned roles.
Bodily dispositions and experience jointly affect stress sensitivity.
Opportunity and incentives encourage the development of interests.
Risk-taking depends on personal disposition and learned incentives.
Family responsibility and institutions cultivate cooperation.
Empathy combines human capacities with moral formation.
Attention reflects ability and learning conditions without a doctrine-wide ranking.
Moral habits are transmitted through family and civic responsibility.
Experience of insecurity and education shape perceived threats.
Temperament involves individual constitution and development.
Taste combines embodied inclinations with experience and convention.
Neither individualism nor national character claims establish a racial genetic crime explanation.
Responsibility is cultivated through conduct and upbringing, not racial inheritance.
Productivity and choices affect pay, while opportunities and expectations also matter.

review.reviewer: Codex independent assessment reviewer /root/socialist_green (separate from author)
review.notes: Independently read all 240 answers against the current bank and checked the scoped primary doctrine plus scholarship/context. No scores or desired locations were consulted. Reviewed literal government authority, ownership versus funding, official religious review versus veto, graduate routes versus guaranteed residence, military initiation versus response, and causal claims versus moral equality. Corrections: restricted-immigration-open-immigration-12: 1 -> 1; militarist-pacifist-12: 0 -> 1. The inferred modern-policy answers and mixed causal models remain representative applications, not documented answers by every adherent or scientific causal estimates. Similarity review is a subsequent mechanical check. Checked the retrospective 1992 principles speech, ownership history and 1980 right-to-buy context; historical actions do not imply a current incumbent government embodies Thatcherism. Validation returned zero errors. Explicitly examined neutral-count warnings: assimilation-multiculturalism 7/16, restricted-immigration-open-immigration 5/16, secular-religious 6/16, central-local 5/16, culture-nature 11/16. Retained condition-dependent policy tradeoffs and representative interaction models; in particular the Culture vs Nature neutrals withhold causal primacy rather than converting equal rights into empirical proof. High neutrality records weaker doctrinal determination and must not be presented as a precisely measured consensus among adherents. No answers were changed after inspecting validation scores.
